items.title: Topical Questions
items.text: Teachers at Beckley Church of England primary school in my constituency, as well as parents of pupils, have contacted me to talk about the severe impact of the Government’s reforms of the way in which physical education is funded in schools on the school’s provision, in which there has been a massive drop. I am sure that that is not the intention of the reforms, but will the Minister agree to meet me to discuss what is happening in Beckley and at other schools?

items.title: Topical Questions
items.text: The potential for deep geothermal projects to provide transition jobs for oil and gas workers in this country continues to be tragically under-utilised. Will the Minister meet me and the hon. Member for Bishop Auckland (Dr Rushworth), as co-chairs of the APPG on deep geothermal, to discuss how we can use a North sea wealth fund to fix that?

items.title: Rosebank Oilfield
items.text: On Rosebank, the hon. Lady talks about the consequences of the climate heating. What percentage contribution will Rosebank make to the global warming of this country?

items.title: Rosebank Oilfield
items.text: Are we not at risk of swapping one set of vulnerabilities in relation to oil and gas and a country like Russia with another set of vulnerabilities in relation to a country like China, given its dominance of critical mineral supplies and solar panel manufacturing? We will be just as insecure, just in a different way.

items.title: UK-EU Relations
items.text: The Minister mentions Ukraine, which we have talked about today. Not having the arrangements with the EU that the Prime Minister is seeking in absolutely no way dampened our ability to work with Europe on Ukraine. We have been able to work together, and stand up strongly for Ukraine, under existing arrangements. What is so bad about them?

items.title: UK-EU Relations
items.text: I thank my hon. Friend for raising the point about how the EU behaves. I have such a strong sense of déjà vu. During the original negotiation period, every time that the EU was obstinate, stubborn and difficult, Labour Members sought to blame the Conservatives for that, instead of getting behind this country and standing up to that sort of behaviour.

items.title: Welfare
items.text: I do not think that foreign nationals should be entitled to benefits, because of the basis on which they are allowed into our country. The only reason they are allowed into our country is that they are net contributors. Why would we undermine that by allowing them to be net recipients of benefits? They are only here because they have signed up to the idea that they will come and be net contributors, so I do not think that that entitles them.

items.title: Welfare
items.text: That is not the system that we propose. We are talking about people who have had an opportunity to contribute and have not done so; the system should take that into account. That is a fair and reasonable point to make.

items.text: Let me finish my point. The fact is that mental health conditions are almost entirely self-reported. items.text: I have a solemn duty to talk about an incredibly difficult and challenging statistic in relation to the prosperity of this country: the size and scale of worklessness in our country right now. items.text: On employers, there are various, complex ways in which the Government are trying to unpick the damage they did with their tax rises. items.text: The Minister is berating us on the question of spending during our time in government, arguing that we did not bring it down, but can he name a single one of those years in which the Labour Opposition asked us to bring it down?

business.title: Finance, Performance and Risk Monitoring Report – Q2
business.text: 1. The forecast revenue outturn position for 2026/27, and the actions within the conclusion and management action section, be noted. 2. The detailed capital programme monitoring be noted, and 3. The analysis of the Council’s achievement re the PIER (Priority Income, and Expenditure Review) savings in 2026/27, be noted as reviewed.

business.title: Treasury Management Update – 2026/27 Quarter 2
business.text: Cabinet resolved to RECOMMEND to Full Council: 1. The report and the assurances contained within, that activities have been in accordance with the approved Treasury Management strategy.

business.title: Fees & Charges 2027/28
business.text: Cabinet resolved to RECOMMEND to Full Council: To approve the proposed 2027/28 fees and charges on existing services to be implemented from 1 April 2027 as annotated on Appendix A.

business.title: External Funding and Grant Applications
business.text: 1. To note the successful securing of external funding totalling approximately £2.12 million for heritage, leisure and regeneration projects across Hastings. 2. To accept £1.3 million from the Lawn Tennis Association and its charitable funding partner organisation for the development of covered tennis and padel facilities at White Rock Gardens. 3.

business.title: Age Friendly Hastings Strategy & Action Plan
business.text: 1. To approve the Age Friendly Hastings Strategy, Action Plan and Evaluation Framework. 2. To endorse the strategy and action plan ensuring cross-council delivery and external support where appropriate 3. This programme is funded by Public Health and receives £50,000 per annum (2025 2028).

business.title: Museum minutes and recommendations
business.text: To note and approve the recommendations of the Museum Committee meeting held on 14 September 2026.

business.title: Extension to election printing contract (Items 11 & 13 taken in open session)
business.text: 1. To approve the extension of the election printing contract considering the current pause on the Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) timetable and ensure continued election printing services to 2028. 2. Agree the contract terms, subject to the financial considerations as set out in Part 2 of the report. 3.

business.title: Special Urgency - Delivering Residents' priorities through investment in playgrounds
business.text: 1. To note the award of £270,000 funding through the Ministry of Housing Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) Playground Fund. 2. To approve the use of £1.0 million of Pride in Place Impact Fund allocation together with the £270,000 MHCLG Playground Fund allocation and £280,000 of existing Council capital funding for a borough-wide playground improvement programme. 3.

business.title: Council Tax and Business Rates Collection and Recovery Activity
business.text: It was agreed by the Chair to vary the order of the Agenda and for Members to discuss Item 6 before Item 5. In June, the Audit Committee (AC) considered a report highlighting delays in the Valuation Office Agency’s (VO) Council Tax (CT) banding notifications. The AC, therefore requested an update, along with information on cases being progressed through the Magistrates’ Court and collection rate data for 2025/26.

business.title: External Audit - Audit Findings Report 2025/26
business.text: Members received the report of the Director of Resources, which summarised the Audit Findings Report (AFR) for 2025/26 prepared by the Council’s external auditor, Grant Thornton (GT), on its audit of the Statement of Accounts for 2025/26. The Committee had considered the Annual Audit Report, which examined the Council’s arrangements for achieving value for money, at its meeting in September.

business.title: Statement of Accounts 2025/26
business.text: Members received the report of the Director of Resources on the Statement of Accounts 2025/26, which provided commentary on the core financial statements. Following the external audit, the updated Statement of Accounts had been published on the Council’s website and included at Appendix A to the report.
